title: Bringing Generative AI to Adaptive Learning in Education
extended_summary:
This position paper addresses how generative AI, especially large language models and diffusion models, could be integrated into adaptive learning systems in education. The authors argue that generative AI can complement and extend current machine-learning-based adaptive learning approaches, particularly in learner profiling, knowledge tracing, computerized adaptive testing, material recommendation, content creation, intelligent tutoring/agent functions, and learning simulation. The paper is motivated by the rapid growth of generative AI and the established effectiveness of adaptive learning, but notes that no prior work had systematically focused on their intersection.

The paper does not report an empirical study with participants. Instead, it synthesizes prior research and industrial examples to outline three major directions: empowering existing adaptive learning algorithms and establishing novel ones. It discusses how generative AI may improve dynamic question generation, add external knowledge, support personalized recommendations, enable multimodal instructional content, and act as an intelligent agent for feedback and planning. It also highlights possible roles for synthetic student data and role-play simulations to address data scarcity in educational settings.

The context is broadly K-12 and higher education, but the discussion is general rather than tied to a specific population or school setting. The authors conclude that generative AI could significantly advance adaptive learning by making systems more dynamic, personalized, and capable, while also warning about risks such as hallucination, fairness, capability decay, and governance concerns. The paper frames these issues as open research questions rather than evaluating a deployed intervention.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a position paper with no original empirical evaluation, no experimental design, and no measured student outcomes. It is useful for theory-building and scoping but does not provide direct evidence of effectiveness.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper argues for potentially meaningful future impact of GenAI-enhanced adaptive learning, but it reports no observed effect sizes or implemented intervention outcomes. Its practical impact remains speculative rather than demonstrated.

interventions.use_case: positioning large language models as adaptive learning tutors, student learning assistants, and instructor agents for real-time question answering, feedback, planning, and role-play-based learning simulation

adaptive learning systems that personalize content, sequencing, learner profiling, and material recommendation using student interaction data; the paper discusses adding generative AI to enhance these adaptive pipelines
GenAI-based automatic feedback and grading support for student assignments, especially general-format questions and written work
classical adaptive tutoring components such as knowledge tracing, computerized adaptive testing, and learner modeling that GenAI is proposed to augment
